newsitem.title: USA: Waterhouse says Fed extends merger review.
newsitem.headline: Waterhouse says Fed extends merger review.

text.p: Waterhouse Investor Services Inc said the U.S. Federal Reserve has extended its review of the company's pending merger with Toronto-Dominion Bank, a development almost certain to delay closing of the deal.

Richard Neiman, general counsel for Waterhouse, said the wait period was extended so the Fed could consider a consumer activist group's opposition to the merger and Waterhouse's response to the group's charge that a company unit failed to comply with the U.S. Community Reinvestment Act.
"We received our last request for information on August 20 and responded fully on August 21," Neiman said in a telephone interview. "We feel we have a pretty strong record on CRA."
Neiman said that although he could not predict the outcome of the review, the Fed had not indicated to Waterhouse any intention of blocking the merger.
"No issues were raised with respect to denial", Neiman said. He also called "unlikely" the prospect of the Federal Reserve attaching a number of contingencies to the deal.
"If there were concerns, they would have been raised a long time ago," he said.

Waterhouse and Toronto-Dominion had hoped to complete the merger by September 16. However, because the deal cannot close until 15 days after receipt of Fed approval, and because the extension to the wait period runs 31 days from August 25, that target is now likely to be missed, Neiman said.
"We plan on closing as soon as is practical after receipt of Federal Reserve approval," he said, noting the Fed's decision could come before the end of the wait period.
